options.text: differences in opportunity cost
the absolute size of a country's population
the colour of a country's currency
the number of commercial banks in the capital

questions.explanation: A country has a comparative advantage where its opportunity cost is lower. That, not absolute productivity or population size, is why specialisation and trade can raise welfare for both partners.

distractorRationale.b: A large population may affect market size, but it does not define comparative advantage
distractorRationale.c: The appearance of notes is irrelevant to the theory of trade
distractorRationale.d: The banking structure is a monetary-system fact, not the basis of trade

options.text: visible exports minus visible imports
the difference between government revenue and expenditure
M1 plus M2
GDP minus depreciation

questions.explanation: The balance of trade, or visible balance, records merchandise only. Services, income and capital flows belong in the wider balance of payments. Budget balance, money supply and NNP are different concepts.

distractorRationale.b: Revenue minus expenditure is the budget balance
distractorRationale.c: M1 and M2 are measures of the money supply
distractorRationale.d: GDP minus depreciation is closer to NDP, a national-income aggregate

questions.stem: A Nigerian worker can produce 8 bags of cocoa or 4 bolts of cloth per month. What is the opportunity cost of one bag of cocoa, in bolts of cloth?
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost of one bag of cocoa is cloth given up divided by cocoa produced: 4/8 = 0.5 bolt. That is the figure compared across countries to locate comparative advantage. Taking 8/4 = 2 would be the opportunity cost of a bolt of cloth, not of a bag of cocoa.

questions.stem: Which of the following is recorded on the current account of the balance of payments?

options.text: Exports of crude oil and imports of machinery
A foreign firm building a new factory as direct investment
The issue of a 10-year Eurobond
The purchase of shares on the NGX by a foreign portfolio investor

questions.explanation: Goods exports and imports are the visible trade component of the current account. A new factory, a Eurobond issue and portfolio purchases of shares are capital and financial account items: they create or change claims, they are not current earnings from trade.

distractorRationale.b: Foreign direct investment belongs on the financial account
distractorRationale.c: Issuing a Eurobond is long-term borrowing, a capital/financial inflow
distractorRationale.d: Portfolio investment is a financial-account transaction

options.text: a tax on imported goods
a complete ban on trade
a physical limit on the quantity imported
the printing of extra naira by the CBN

questions.explanation: A tariff is a customs duty: it raises the price of the import and earns revenue. A complete ban is an embargo, a quantity cap is a quota, and printing naira is monetary policy, not a commercial-policy instrument.

distractorRationale.b: A complete ban is an embargo
distractorRationale.c: A quantity limit is a quota
distractorRationale.d: Currency issue is a CBN function, unrelated to import protection

questions.stem: Devaluation of the naira is intended to correct a balance-of-payments deficit by

options.text: making exports cheaper in foreign currency and imports dearer in naira
raising the naira's value so that imports become cheaper
increasing the cash reserve ratio of commercial banks
banning all capital-account transactions permanently

questions.explanation: A lower naira means a dollar buys more naira, so Nigerian goods look cheaper abroad and foreign goods look dearer at home. If export and import volumes respond enough, the current account improves. Revaluation would cheapen imports, and CRR is a monetary tool rather than an exchange-rate tool.

distractorRationale.b: That describes a revaluation or appreciation, which tends to worsen a deficit
distractorRationale.c: Raising CRR is monetary tightening; it may cut imports indirectly but is not what devaluation means
distractorRationale.d: Exchange control may accompany a deficit strategy, but devaluation is a price change, not a permanent capital ban
